extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, and examiners involved in Korean patent prosecution (KIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing preliminary examination interviews, pre-amendment communication interviews, and collective examination requests at the Korean Patent Office, including who may participate, required records, timelines, and examiner/applicant responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner explanation of review during preliminary examination interview
rubrics_metrics.description: The result of the review shall be explained to applicant during the preliminary examination interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should orally explain grounds for rejection based on review (requirements for patentability, deficiencies in the specification, etc.). It is appropriate to prepare an opinion in advance, but grounds should be explained verbally during the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may suggest amendments but not order applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a proper way to resolve grounds for rejection, it will be appropriate for the examiner to actively suggest it to the applicant during the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the examiner suggests an amendment, the examiner shall not order or lead the applicant to follow it; must explain that (1) the suggestion has no legal binding force and final decision rests with the applicant, and (2) the suggestion can change according to new prior art or evidence discovered after interview or amendment after interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion on possible amendment to secure proper scope of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner and the applicant shall make effort to consult possible amendment to resolve grounds for rejection and to secure proper scope of a patent based on advice and preliminary amendment proposed by each party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to state all contents discussed and agreed in minutes. If no agreement is reached, statement of amendment discussed can be omitted. Examiner can suggest language but cannot force applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews should not be used mainly for simple process inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple contact for information, question of progress of examination, and process of patent, etc., do not meet the purpose of preliminary examination and are not allowed to be main contents of interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such matters may be included but should not be the main focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes of interview must be prepared, signed, and uploaded
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant and the examiner who participated in the interview shall prepare the minutes after finishing the interview and sign to prove checking the contents of the minutes. The minutes with sign shall be uploaded to the Patent Net to add it to examination history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After signing, a copy can be distributed to the applicant upon request. Computerized interview report must be identical to the minutes; include an image of applicant-signed minutes to indicate confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in interview minutes/record
rubrics_metrics.description: In the minutes of interview, interview date, place, application number, title of invention, name of participant, examiner’s opinion on grounds for rejection, and suggestion of amendment discussed, etc. shall be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is enough to state the purpose/summary of the grounds for rejection for reference during/after interview; applicant's responses and any suggestions or agreed amendment language should be recorded when discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stating opinion on grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Opinion on grounds for rejection’ is about results of review of the claimed invention conducted by examiner considering requirements for patentability and deficiency in the specification, and applicant’s response to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should prepare the opinion in advance and participate with it, but must orally explain grounds during interview. Minutes may summarize the purpose of the grounds for rejection; applicant's argument in response shall be described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording suggestion of amendment discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the suggestion of amendment proposed by the examiner to resolve grounds for rejection is discussed by the examiner and the applicant, the result of discussion shall be stated in the minutes of interview to make it a record of examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If specific amendment language is agreed, record it. Recommended to state all contents discussed and agreed. If no agreement is reached, statement of amendment discussed can be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions allowing examiner to finish interview early
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner may finish the interview when the object is accomplished and minutes prepared; examiner can finish by notifying applicant in certain cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible early finish cases include: (①) interview goes beyond original purpose, (②) applicant presents multiple preliminary amendments and asks for examiner’s opinion, (③) impossible to achieve agreement or communication problems, (④) time becomes unnecessarily long, (⑤) impossible to have effective interview. If finished early, only matters discussed before finish need be included in minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must prepare written amendment/arguments after interview
rubrics_metrics.description: An agent (if not, applicant) shall prepare written amendment to the specification or arguments after interview by reflecting applicant’s opinion on the amendment discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment stated in minutes is a matter discussed between examiner and applicant, but applicant may freely amend regardless of minutes and submit written arguments. If applicant wants to amend according to discussed amendment before substantive examination start, submit written amendment within specified period (within 10 days from due date of start — typically 2 months from request for preliminary examination; 4 months for PPH/expedited). Extensions may be requested by telephone for inevitable reasons. It is not permitted to present simplified arguments assuming interview discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must prepare interview report and add minutes to prosecution history
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner shall prepare an interview report through the patent system after finishing the interview to add the minutes prepared during the interview to the examination history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computerized contents shall be identical to the minutes. Include the minutes with applicant's signature as an image to show confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of substantive examination after interview
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examiner starts substantive examination based on contents (amendment discussed, etc.) stated in the minutes of interview when due date for start of substantive examination has arrived, but shall postpone until period for submitting written amendment of preliminary examination is expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If written amendment is not submitted within the period, examiner commences substantive examination within 2 months from date to request preliminary examination (4 months for PPH/accelerated). If written amendment filed before substantive examination, examiner can proceed within a month from receiving date. Examiner may make different decisions if new prior art or deficiencies are discovered after interview; for simple grounds may request voluntary amendment by telephone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of pre-amendment communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-amendment communication is a system to exchange opinions on draft amendment between applicants and examiners through the interview before submitting amendment in response to the outstanding rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It contributes to early allowance opportunities and helps examiners carry out more accurate examination. Process steps include submitting draft amendment, requesting pre-amendment communication, determination, interview, submission of written amendment, and expiration of amendment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for pre-amendment communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Among applications with grounds for rejection notified by an examiner, an application for which arguments including amendment or draft amendment are submitted before a month from the expiration date of submission period for arguments may be eligible for pre-amendment communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should submit draft amendment/arguments within the time window to be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request and who may participate in pre-amendment communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants or agents are allowed to request for pre-amendment communication. Persons who can participate include the person in charge who can respond to office action (applicant/representative, agent, subagent empowered to appoint a subagent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications represented by an agent, the agent should participate. Inventor may participate but must be with applicant/agent or person empowered. For assistant examiner-handled applications, supervising examiner should also participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of matters discussable in pre-amendment interview
rubrics_metrics.description: All matters that help to resolve grounds for rejection notified and to secure proper scope of right based on draft amendment submitted by an applicant can be discussed in the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may explain how amendment resolves grounds with technical explanations and use samples/multimedia; examiner may present preliminary opinion whether draft amendment resolves grounds and suggest further amendment. Both consult about appropriate amendment to secure proper scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and method to request pre-amendment communication
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for pre-amendment communication should be filed before a month from the expiration date of the period for submitting written amendment pursuant to the Notice of grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To file, applicant visits Patent-Ro and fills name, application number, desired interview date, participant, contact, and whether to submit draft amendment. Applicant should choose 3 desired interview dates within 2–3 weeks from request (select 3 days) considering review/preparation time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner determination timeframe and requirements for pre-amendment requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a request, the examiner should accept or reject the request through Patent Net within 7 days from the request date. To decide, examiner should consider specific requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: (①) submission of draft amendment at or before request (examiner should confirm via prosecution history or contact Application Division/applicant if delayed); (②) request filed before one month from expiration date; (③) appropriate interview participants; (④) desired interview date includes 3 candidate dates within 2–3 weeks; (⑤) check for inappropriate grounds such as multiple pre-amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance, conditional acceptance, and return of pre-amendment request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request satisfies requirements, the examiner shall accept it and choose an interview date among proposed dates. If the request lacks a requirement but deficiency can be resolved by discussion, examiner may accept ex officio. If deficiency cannot be resolved, the request can be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If returned, applicant may file again within the period after resolving deficiencies. Examiner should consult with applicant to determine date if none of proposed dates work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay or cancellation of interview by applicant/examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has an inevitable reason not to attend, the examiner may give one chance to select another date among available dates within 15–21 days from request; if examiner considers reason inappropriate, the interview can be canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one opportunity to reschedule is normally granted; examiner discretion applies for cancellations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner preparation for pre-amendment interview
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should review whether grounds for rejection are resolved, whether new grounds occur, and so on based on draft amendment submitted; review should be comparable to examination to explain clearly in the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should participate with application documents, draft amendment, preview results, and bring written interview record and additional paper to record consultation matters. Recommended to state result of pre-amendment communication in the written interview record in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings during pre-amendment interview: applicant explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should explain draft amendment submitted to the examiner before (or at the time of) requesting review of draft amendment, focusing on whether grounds for rejection are resolved and possibly giving technical explanations and prior art discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may use samples or multimedia (photos, videos, etc.); examiner can require interview materials in advance if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings during pre-amendment interview: examiner preview and suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: After pre-amendment review is determined, the examiner should carry out preview and explain the result to the applicant in the interview; examiner can suggest amendment if necessary to resolve grounds or secure appropriate scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preview should assess whether draft amendment resolves notified grounds and whether new grounds arise. Examiner's suggestions are advisory and non-binding; explain that opinion may change with new prior art or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written interview record requirements for pre-amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant and examiner should prepare written interview record after interview and sign it; record should be uploaded to the examination history (Patent-Net).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written interview record includes interview date, place, application number, title, participants, result of pre-amendment review, and discussed amendment. For 'result of pre-amendment review', a summary of grounds may suffice; applicant's opinion should be recorded. If applicant agrees with proposed amendment, the result and agreed language should be stated; if no agreement, amendment statement may be omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-pre-amendment applicant obligations and freedoms
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent/applicant should prepare written amendment or argument reflecting applicant’s opinion on consulted amendment after interview, but may freely make amendment regardless of the consulted amendment recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant wants to adopt consulted amendment, submit written amendment by the expiration date of amendment period. It is not permitted to summarize written argument assuming interview content without filing full argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner post-interview processing for pre-amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should prepare interview report via Patent Net to upload the written interview record; computerized contents must match the written record and include applicant-signed image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After interview, examiner conducts examination considering consulted amendment per normal process and periods for office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective examination purpose and overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective examination is a system to carry out examination collectively on a date an applicant desires for multiple applications (patent, utility model, trademark, design) relating to one product to support portfolio timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables companies to obtain patents for a product at a desired time (e.g., before product release) and to establish a portfolio of IP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request collective examination and representative selection
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for collective examination should be filed by the applicant; if there are more than two applicants, one must be selected as representative to make the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner fills the request form via Patent-Ro and attaches required certified documents; documents proving practice or preparation may be shown during presentation if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for collective examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more applications (patent/utility model/trademark/design) for which substantive examination has not started and satisfying either (1) applications relating to one product and meeting one of listed requirements, or (2) related to development from identical national new technology support project, are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements under (1) include: practicing/preparing for practicing, export promotion-related, company confirmed as venture business or selected SME, or related to fostering self-employed creative enterprises. Patent and utility model limited to those for which a request for examination is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective examination scheduling and request timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner designates a desired candidate date for presentation (7–14 days after request), desired start date for collective examination (after 14 days from presentation), and desired finishing date (within one year after 3 months from desired start).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preliminary examination is wanted, it can be requested when filing. After the request, some applications may be withdrawn but not changed or added.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination procedure for collective examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Official in charge must confirm eligibility and procedural requirements; if request does not satisfy requirements, notify petitioner to amend within 6 days, or the request cannot be permitted or offending application may be excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official in charge should consult petitioner and examiner in charge to select holding date of presentation and notify petitioner of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation for collective examination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner must participate in the presentation at the confirmed date to explain the applications and that they relate to one product; Official in charge and examiner in charge consult whether applications satisfy requirements and determine start/finish dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official in charge notifies petitioner of determined matters. If preliminary examination was requested, preliminary interview/process follows same rules as earlier chapters.
